text:
alex: Kicking off sa-east1 GPU pool bring-up (A10G). Nodes created but node-provisioner shows repeated CNI errors. Anyone else seeing this?
priya: I see a ton of ENI detach/attach in cloud logs and kubelet flaps. Pod networking failing on init containers.
luis: `dmesg` shows: "NETDEV WATCHDOG: eth0: transmit queue 0 timed out" — also PMTU warnings in calico.
infra-oncall: SRE-bot alerted: deploy-gpu-pool-23 failed healthcheck, rolling back to previous ASG
sre-bot: [alert] autoscaler: failed to scale up target group 'gpu-pool-sae' - instance provisioning timeout
alex: paste logs from one failing node:
```
May 12 12:03:11 kubelet[1234]: kubelet: network plugin returns error: cni plugin timed out
May 12 12:03:12 calico[567]: ERROR: failed to set route: Message too long
May 12 12:03:13 kernel: IPv4: packet too big: PMTU 1500 -> 1436
```
priya: config check: we set MTU 1450 on VPC peering but nodes default to 1500. That could explain fragmentation / cni failures.
marie: Also the GPU AMI build used docker runtime runc v1.1 while our cluster image uses runc v1.2; some node boot scripts failed silently.
luis: So two problems: MTU mismatch causing CNI flaps, and AMI mismatch causing kubelet/driver install race. Which to fix first?
alex: Quick mitigation: pin MTU to 1450 in cni config, and switch new ASG to the previous AMI (non-GPU) to restore control plane. Can we do that now?
infra-oncall: Changing launch template to prev-AMI and triggering ASG replace now. ETA 8m :hourglass_flowing_sand:
priya: I'll push a small Calico config change to set 'mtu: 1450' and a DaemonSet to drain & reconfigure existing nodes gradually.
sre-bot: Deploy note: canary replacement will run on 2 nodes at a time.
alex: Cost note: we planned preemptible A10G to save $; if we keep falling back to non-GPU AMI during boot, we need a manual cost watch. tagging the run to billing-alerts.
marie: After rollback started, control plane stabilized. Kubelet Ready went from 60% -> 95% in 12 minutes.
luis: Next steps: (1) bake GPU AMI with latest runc + driver install ordering fix, (2) update CNI MTU in infra repo and cloud routes, (3) run small AB of 10 nodes to validate.
alex: Agreed. I'll open a follow-up postmortem with action items and owners. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
